text.p: Toreador Royalty Corp said Friday Apache Corp has agreed to an option farmout covering some 22,500 acres located on the Matador Arch, Motley County, Texas.
Toreador will not be fully carried under the agreement, Chairman Peter R. Vig told Reuters, but he declined to say how much money the company would have to raise for the program.

Toreador's statement said Apache is the operator for the venture and has a 56.25 percent working interest. Toreador retains a 43.75 percent working interest as well as a 15 percent royalty interest in the majority of the acreage.

The company has a 75 percent mineral ownership in the tract, which is located north and east of the three-field Roaring Springs complex which has produced in excess of nine million barrels of oil from Wolfcamp (Permian) reefs at depths of less than 4,500 feet.

Apache is expected to commence the initial phase of the 3-D seismic survey covering 9,500 acres no later than mid-May, Vig said. The five-well Matador Field, a Wolfcamp reef discovery made by Toreador and its partners in 1994, is included in this initial survey.
Assuming positive results from the survey, drilling of the first well should start in August or September, he said.
"Based upon our large working and royalty interest, this is a very significant project for Toreador," Vig added.
He said the company assembled the acerage, and provided regional geology and 2D seismic to the venture.
